text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT: High GPU queue growth for private cluster 'acme-vpc-2'. Autoscaler failed to provision new nodes. Customer traffic is queueing and observed 503s. Paging oncall. thread=1767423600

ana (oncall): ack, I'm on it. Paging infra and SRE.

maria (cs): FYI: ACME reported increased error rates on their private endpoint ~10:42 UTC, some jobs timing out. They're seeing spikes in latency and internal queue length.

jason (infra): looking now — can you share the span of errors / logs?

maria (cs): sending links to their metrics dashboard and sample traces: https://redwood.metrics/acme/private/requests?span=30m

ana (oncall): grabbing autoscaler status from the operator.

ana (oncall): ```
# kubectl -n redwood get hpa,verticalpodautoscaler,clusterautoscaler -o wide
NAME                              READY   TARGETS   MINPODS   MAXPODS   REPLICAS
cluster-autoscaler                True    -         0         20        20
\n# kubectl -n redwood describe clusterautoscaler cluster-autoscaler
Events:
  10:41:03  Normal  ScaleUpFailed  Unable to scale up: provider returned error: InsufficientCapacity
  10:42:10  Warning ScaleUpLimitReached  Hit cluster max node limit (20)
```

jason (infra): autoscaler reports two issues: provider InsufficientCapacity (cloud couldn't provision GPU instances) and we hit the configured max nodes (20). For this private cluster we have hard limits due to customer VPC policy.

li (sre): queue growth observed in the inference queue monitor: queued requests +420% over 10m, token backlog increasing. Router started returning 503s after queue > 1000.

maria (cs): ACME says they can't accept rerouting to hosted endpoints for compliance — private-only.

ana (oncall): summary: can't autoscale further (max nodes reached) + provider capacity shortage. Need live mitigation and customer impact assessment. Options: 1) increase cluster max (requires customer approval and VPC quota changes), 2) request provider to prioritize (rare), 3) drain low-priority work and shed load, 4) manual node provisioning if possible.

jason (infra): checking nodepool config and recent deploys — no recent config changes. Looks like our default node template requests a specific GPU SKU (a40-32g) that is constrained in the customer's region. We can try a fallback node type but that requires customer opt-in because their private template is locked.

li (sre): immediate mitigation: throttle low-priority tenant jobs and prioritize ACME traffic. We can adjust queue routing TTLs and drop retries.

ana (oncall): applying throttling policy to non-critical jobs now. ```
# curl -X POST https://internal-router/_admin/throttle -d '{"selector":"priority:low","rate":0.1}'
{"status":"applied"}
```

deploy-bot: :gear: config change applied in route 'private-inference-router' by ana at 10:44 UTC.

li (sre): after throttle, queued requests dropped ~30% within 2m. Latency still high for some ACME requests.

jason (infra): contacting customer ops to request temporary increase of node pool max and permission to allow fallback GPU SKU. maria / cs-rep can you coordinate?

cs-rep: pinging ACME ops now. Request: temporarily allow fallback GPU SKU or bump node quota to 30 for the next 6 hours. Waiting on approval.

maria (cs): ACME say they need justification and will accept a temporary increase to 28 nodes if we document security controls. They're on a 3rd-party managed VPC so we need to send an SOW addendum.

ana (oncall): while approvals are pending, can we reduce batch sizes / enable KV cache more aggressively per-request to reduce GPU pressure?

li (sre): yes — pushing runtime config for smaller batch windows and prefer cache hits. ```
# PATCH /runtime/config
{ "batching": { "max_batch_time_ms": 25, "max_batch_tokens": 512 }, "kv_cache": { "prefetch": true }
}
```

deploy-bot: runtime config rollout succeeded (canary 10% -> 100%) at 10:50 UTC.

li (sre): cache changes helped — per-token GPU utilization down ~18%, but overall queue still > 600. Still below normal but not sufficient.

jason (infra): provider support replied — there is a temporary regional shortage of our preferred GPU SKU. They can offer other SKUs but requires node template change in customer's account. That's why ACME approval needed.

maria (cs): ACME legal reviewing addendum now, ETA 30m. They agreed to open temporary escalation to their cloud admin.

ana (oncall): manual short-term step: I'm going to add a single extra non-GPU control-plane node group to host routing and light-weight models to offload some traffic. That doesn't help GPU-bound inference but may reduce overhead. Executing now.```

ana (oncall): ```
# gcloud compute instance-groups managed resize acme-inference-controllers --size=3
Resized from 2 to 3
```

deploy-bot: controller nodegroup scaled to 3 at 10:58 UTC.

li (sre): controller scale reduced router CPU pressure, request fanout improved a bit. Queued inference still high.

jason (infra): once ACME approves changing GPU SKU we can provision mixed nodepool: add 6 nodes with alt SKU and cordon them for inference-only. I'll prepare terraform patch; need customer approve to run in their account.

maria (cs): ACME ops just approved emergency increase to 28 nodes and allowed fallback SKU for the next 4 hours, but they want logs and audit trail after. They asked that any changes be executed by their cloud admin.

cs-rep: coordinating with ACME cloud admin to run our prepared terraform. They requested the exact plan before execution. Jason, can you paste the plan here?

jason (infra): plan (sanitized): ```
+ resource "node_pool" "fallback-gpu" {
+   count = 6
+   instance_type = "a40-alt"
+   taints = ["gpu=true:NoSchedule"]
+ }
```

cs-rep: ACME admin will run after verifying. They estimate ~12-15m to provision.

li (sre): in parallel, we should set a fallback policy to drop best-effort requests when queue > 800 to avoid router meltdown. Nana, can you add?

ana (oncall): adding fail-open policy now. ```
# routerctl set-policy --drop-threshold 800 --drop-targets "priority:best-effort"
Policy updated
```

deploy-bot: router policy updated at 11:12 UTC.

li (sre): immediate effect: queue trend reversed and is slowly decreasing. We are still throttling some jobs. Error rate for ACME is down from 14% -> 6% after fallback nodes come online (partial).

maria (cs): ACME confirms some traffic successfully processed via fallback nodes. They're happy with the progress but want ETA for full recovery.

jason (infra): ACME admin reports fallback nodepool created and 4/6 nodes Ready at 11:26 UTC; autoscaler now sees capacity. We'll drain some low-priority pods onto the new nodes after taint tolerations applied.

li (sre): running graceful pod evict to reschedule onto new nodes. ```
# kubectl -n inference get pods -o wide | grep low-priority | awk '{print $1}' | xargs -n1 kubectl delete pod --grace-period=30
```

ana (oncall): after moving workloads, queue length back to normal (~<150) at 11:35 UTC. ACME error rate down to baseline.

maria (cs): ACME ops: "Thanks for the quick coordination. Please send our teams the audit log and a short playbook so we can avoid this in future."

ana (oncall): writing immediate post-incident actions: 1) follow up with ACME on formal quota increase and addendum, 2) update Private deployment quickstart to include fallback SKU opt-in, 3) add autoscaler alert for 'max nodes reached' with runbook, 4) evaluate region SKU redundancy and default node templates.

jason (infra): I'll open infra ticket to parameterize node SKU and make fallback opt-in less manual.

li (sre): will prepare an alert that notifies oncall when queue growth >200% and cluster-autoscaler reports ScaleUpLimitReached for >5m. Also add an automated mitigation to throttle low-priority jobs earlier.

maria (cs): I'll prepare customer-facing summary and the audit package for ACME.

ana (oncall): handing off to night oncall — li will take over monitoring and runbook follow-ups. I'll produce the incident timeline and handoff notes.

li (sre): taking over. I'm oncall until 08:00 UTC. I'll monitor queues and confirm final remediation tasks.

ana (oncall): thanks team. Incident mitigated, customer impacted but recovered. Creating postmortem ticket and will assign owners. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident status updated to 'mitigated' at 11:45 UTC. Postmortem ticket: https://redwood.tracker/INC-3752
